lessons.title: Target Interception using Proxy Traps (get, set, apply)
lessons.description: Proxies intercept operations on objects — customizing behavior for property access, assignment and function calls.

sections.heading: What is a Proxy?
paragraphs: A Proxy wraps an object and intercepts fundamental operations. You can customize what happens when properties are read, written, deleted or functions are called.
list: new Proxy(target, handler) — creates a proxied object
handler traps: get, set, has, deleteProperty, apply, etc.
The proxy intercepts operations on the target object
Transparent to most code — proxies behave like regular objects

codeExamples.heading: Proxy get and set traps
explanation: The get trap intercepts every property read on the proxy.
The set trap intercepts every property assignment.
The proxy wraps the original object — operations go through the traps first.
Return true from set to indicate the operation succeeded.

practice.task: Create a proxy that logs every property access and prevents modification of properties starting with underscore (_).
hints: In the get trap: log prop and return the value.
In the set trap: check if prop.startsWith("_").
If it starts with _, throw an error or ignore the set.

keyTakeaways: Proxies intercept fundamental object operations via handler traps.
get, set, has and deleteProperty are the most commonly used traps.
Proxies are transparent — most code doesn't know it's talking to a proxy.
They enable validation, logging, access control and reactive systems.
lessons.challenge: Build a validation proxy that enforces type constraints on object properties.

lessons.title: Default Operation Delegation with the Reflect API
lessons.description: Reflect provides methods that mirror Proxy traps — use it to delegate default behavior cleanly.

sections.heading: What is Reflect?
paragraphs: Reflect is a built-in object with methods that correspond to Proxy traps. Instead of manually manipulating target[prop], use Reflect to perform the default behavior.
list: Always pairs with Proxy for clean delegation

codeExamples.heading: Reflect with Proxy
explanation: Reflect.get/set perform the default operation cleanly.
The handler can modify values before delegating with Reflect.
receiver ensures proper this binding in inheritance chains.
Always use Reflect in Proxy traps for clean, correct delegation.

practice.task: Create a proxy that converts all string values to uppercase when they're set on an object. Use Reflect for default behavior.
hints: In the set trap: check if typeof value === "string".

keyTakeaways: Reflect methods mirror Proxy traps — use them for default behavior.
Always use Reflect in Proxy traps instead of manually manipulating target.
Reflect ensures proper receiver binding for inheritance chains.
Together, Proxy and Reflect enable clean meta-programming.
lessons.challenge: Build a logging proxy that records all property access and modification using Reflect for delegation.

lessons.title: Building Reactive State Systems with Proxies
lessons.description: Use Proxies to create reactive objects that automatically trigger callbacks when state changes.

sections.heading: Reactive programming with Proxies
paragraphs: Reactive systems automatically update when data changes — the foundation of Vue.js, MobX and other frameworks. Proxies make this possible by intercepting set operations.
list: Intercept set operations to detect state changes
Trigger callbacks or re-renders when data changes
Track which properties are accessed (dependency tracking)
This is how Vue 3's reactivity system works internally

codeExamples.heading: Simple reactive state
explanation: The reactive() function wraps an object in a Proxy.
The set trap detects changes and triggers the callback.
Only actual changes (oldValue !== newValue) trigger notifications.
This is the core pattern behind reactive frameworks.

practice.task: Build a reactive state object that updates a DOM element whenever a property changes.

keyTakeaways: Proxies enable reactive systems by intercepting property changes.
The set trap detects changes and triggers update callbacks.
This is the foundation of Vue 3, MobX and similar frameworks.
Reactive programming eliminates manual DOM updates — the UI reflects the data automatically.
lessons.challenge: Build a mini reactive framework that supports computed properties and watchers using Proxy.
